gate: V38 full local load matrix: diagnostic evidence only; admission timeouts and non-reattachable response stalls remain
limitations: Reattachable and non-reattachable 60-second 1/4/8/16-client cohorts were measured at active-operation limits 2, 4, and 8 against both local and shared Quack owners.

For reattachable runs, both owner modes recorded 25, 19, and 10 admission rejections at active limits 2, 4, and 8. Only active-limit-8 cohorts with 1/4 clients had zero rejections; this is a single-host candidate observation, not a release support guarantee.

For non-reattachable runs, both owner modes recorded 27, 21, and 13 combined admission/stall rejections at active limits 2, 4, and 8. Slow-reader response stalls occurred in every measured active-limit cohort, including the final reader; no non-reattachable supported-load envelope is established.
Across all load runs accepted results were correct, health probes had no errors, and server/owner processes shut down gracefully. Load rejection and stream-stall failures remain unresolved.
The shared-owner lifecycle smoke tests owner restart and recovery, but owner loss during an actively streamed result remains open.
Storage-level COMMIT failure injection and complete release/cleanup acceptance remain open.
Cross-platform execution and exact release-artifact/package checks remain release gates.
